name: TPS259231DRCR
title: TPS25923x: 5 V eFuse with 6.1 V over-voltage clamp and blocking-FET drive
summary: A 5 V electronic fuse with a 28 mΩ internal pass FET, rated to 20 V on VIN. It holds the output at 6.1 V when the input surges, limits current to a level set by one resistor (1 A to 5 A), sets the output ramp with one capacitor, and has an adjustable UVLO and thermal shutdown. A BFET pin drives an external N-channel FET for reverse-current blocking. TPS259231 retries after a thermal fault; TPS259230 latches off. Both come in a 3 mm × 3 mm 10-pin VSON.
key_figures: 4.5 V to 5.5 V; VIN absolute maximum 20 V (22 V for 10 ms)
28 mΩ typ, 37 mΩ max at TJ = 25 °C
1 A to 5 A by RILIM; 3.75 A typ at 100 kΩ

notes: Each also appears with a .A suffix, same package and packing. Operating temperature −40 °C to 85 °C for all.

pins.name: dV/dT
pins.function: Output slew-rate setting. A capacitor to GND slows the rise of OUT when the device turns on; left open, the fastest ramp results.

pins.name: EN/UVLO
pins.function: Enable and undervoltage input. Low turns the pass FET off and pulls BFET to GND; high turns the device and BFET on. A resistor divider from the supply sets a custom UVLO trip level.

pins.name: VIN
pins.function: Supply input; pins 3 to 5 are joined.

pins.name: OUT
pins.function: Protected output; pins 6 to 8 are joined.

pins.name: BFET
pins.function: Gate drive for an optional external N-channel blocking FET. Leave it open when no blocking FET is fitted.

pins.name: ILIM
pins.function: Current-limit setting. A resistor to GND programs the overload and short-circuit limits.

pins.name: GND
pins.function: Ground, the exposed thermal pad (pad 11); reference for every voltage.

circuits.title: Basic eFuse with resistor-set UVLO, ramp and current limit
circuits.description: The minimum circuit. R1 and R2 divide VIN onto EN/UVLO to set the undervoltage trip; CdVdT on dV/dT sets the output ramp; RLIM on ILIM sets the current limit; COUT is the load-side capacitance. BFET is left open, so no blocking FET is used.

circuits.title: Simple 3.7 A eFuse for set-top boxes
circuits.description: A 3.7 A protected rail from a 4.5 V to 18 V input, output under 3.4 A. RILIM = 100 kΩ sets the limit. R1 (1 MΩ) feeds EN/UVLO from VIN with R2 open, so the internal 4.3 V UVLO applies and R1 keeps the EN/UVLO pin current under 20 µA when VIN exceeds the pin's 7 V rating. dV/dT is open for the fastest ramp, about 350 µs at 5 V. CVIN (0.1 µF) is an optional noise filter. BFET is unused.

parts.note: optional, fitted only for an external UVLO level

circuits.title: Inrush and reverse-current protection for a hold-up capacitor (SSD)
circuits.description: A 3 A rail feeding a 4700 µF hold-up capacitor, output under 2.7 A. Q1 (CSD16411, N-channel) sits back to back with the internal FET, source on OUT, drain on VOUT and gate on BFET, so when the input droops the hold-up charge cannot flow back to the source. R1/R2 (1 MΩ / 453 kΩ) set a 4.5 V UVLO and act as the power-fail comparator, with a 4.33 V falling trip, which turns BFET off fast. CdVdT = 22 nF stretches the ramp to about 110 ms, holding inrush to about 213 mA. RILIM = 76.8 kΩ sets 3 A. Q2 (ZXM61P03F, P-channel) has its gate on BFET, its source on the FLTb line and its drain on GND.

circuits.title: Quick output discharge through BFET
circuits.description: When the device is disabled, BFET goes low and turns on Q1 (ZXM61P03F, P-channel), which connects RDCHG from OUT to GND and drains COUT to a defined off state. The discharge rate follows COUT, RDCHG and the load. The rest is the basic circuit: R1/R2 on EN/UVLO, CdVdT, RILIM, and an optional CIN for noise.

circuits.title: Optional transient-suppression parts
circuits.description: The basic circuit with the optional protection parts: CVIN (0.1 µF) and a TVS from VIN to GND clamp the positive spike that input inductance makes when the device cuts the current, and a Schottky from GND to OUT catches the negative spike from output inductance. BFET is unused.

operation.text: The device watches VIN. Once VIN passes the 4.3 V UVLO level (VUVR) it looks at EN/UVLO; a high level there turns on the internal FET and starts charging the gate of an external blocking FET through BFET. The output then rises at the rate set on dV/dT, the fastest rate with dV/dT open. Turn-on delay is 220 µs typ.

EN/UVLO above 1.4 V (VENR) turns the internal FET on and charges BFET; below 1.35 V (VENF) it turns the FET off and pulls the external FET gate to GND through the 26 Ω discharge path. The falling-edge deglitch is about 1 µs, so a divider on EN/UVLO works as a fast power-fail detector that cuts BFET and stops reverse current. A capacitor from EN/UVLO to GND lengthens the deglitch on a noisy supply. Toggling EN/UVLO low then high clears the TPS259230's thermal latch. EN/UVLO is rated to 7 V, so above 7 V it is fed through a resistor (1 MΩ keeps its current under 20 µA).

VIN can sit at up to 20 V continuously. Above the recommended range the device enters over-voltage protection and holds OUT at VOVC, 6.1 V typ, with no external parts. The FET then drops VIN − VOVC at the load current, which heats the part and can end in thermal shutdown.

RILIM sets the overload limit IOL (1 A to 5 A, ±8 % at 3.7 A), which applies once start-up is done. Above 10 W of FET dissipation the limit folds back by 2 % to 12 % to ISC. In either case the FET gate is regulated to hold the current, and over-temperature eventually shuts the device off. With RILIM shorted the limit is about 0.84 A and with it open about 0.73 A (single-point-failure test, UL60950); UL 2367 recognition (file E339631) covers RILIM ≤ 130 kΩ (5 A maximum).

The current-limit amplifier is too slow for a hard short, so a comparator switches the FET off within about 300 ns when the current passes IFASTRIP = 1.6 × IOL. After that peak is cut, the amplifier brings the current back to IOL and regulates it there. The levels stack as IFASTRIP, then IOL, then ISC up to 15 % below it from thermal foldback.

At a junction temperature of 150 °C (TSHDN) the FET is turned off. The TPS259230 stays off until power is cycled or EN/UVLO is toggled. The TPS259231 waits until the junction has cooled 10 °C, then retries after 100 µs, and repeats the cycle until the fault is gone.

BFET drives the gate of an external N-channel FET placed back to back with the output, so that hold-up capacitance cannot discharge through the internal FET's body diode into a failing or shorted input. BFET charges with 2 µA and clamps at VIN + 6.4 V; it discharges through about 26 Ω, switching the external FET off in typically under 1 µs. It charges only when both EN/UVLO is above VENR and VIN is above VUVR. Because the charging current is only 2 µA, a probe on BFET needs more than 10 MΩ impedance.

Disabled, the device leaves OUT floating, so the load alone sets how it powers down. Since BFET goes low on disable, it can switch a P-channel FET that discharges OUT through a resistor (quick output discharge).

Start-up stress is usually much larger than steady-state stress. Pick CdVdT so the start-up dissipation, PD(INRUSH) plus PD(LOAD), lasts less than the thermal shutdown time that the shutdown-time curve gives at the highest ambient. A larger COUT is handled by a larger CdVdT.

CVIN of 0.001 µF to 0.1 µF filters transients, emissions and supply noise. With the source more than a few inches away, an input ceramic above 0.1 µF is used. The supply is rated above the set current limit so it does not droop during overload or short circuit. The design is for 4.5 V ≤ VIN ≤ 18 V.

Cutting the current makes input inductance kick VIN up and output inductance kick OUT negative, by amounts set by those inductances; they can pass the absolute maximum ratings. Remedies: short leads, a large ground plane, a Schottky across the output, a 0.001 µF to 0.1 µF ceramic at the input, and where needed a TVS on the input.

Short-circuit results vary with source bypassing, leads, layout, parts, the way and place the short is made, and the instruments; the short itself bounces and arcs, so waveforms differ from setup to setup.

Put a ceramic of 0.01 µF or more between VIN and GND, right at those pins with the smallest loop; in hot-plug use with negligible input inductance it can be smaller or left off. Make the power path short and wide enough for twice full load. Tie GND to a copper ground plane or island at the pin. Place RILIM, CdVdT and the EN/UVLO resistors next to their pins, return them to the GND pin by the shortest trace, and keep the ILIM and dV/dT traces short and away from switching signals. Place TVS parts, snubbers, capacitors and diodes close to what they protect with short traces; a Schottky for inductive-load negative transients goes close to the OUT pins. Solder the exposed pad to the board.

TPS259230 and TPS259231 share UVLO (4.3 V), clamp (6.1 V) and package; the TPS259230 latches off after a thermal fault and the TPS259231 retries. The TPS259231 ships at MSL 1 and the TPS259230 at MSL 2.
